NPLify · P0 Technical Baseline

Deliverable 1 — Entity-Relationship Diagram & Data Model

New XP Technologies Limited

11 October 2026 · Confidential

Conventions

Convention: all monetary amounts are stored as exact decimals; every table carries created_at / created_by; audit, approvals and locking are modelled once (domain 4) and apply to all master data. Derived figures (client balance, group entitlement, offsets, custody) are views over postings and deals — never stored.

Seven diagrams across four domains, one schema: 70 tables and 12 views. In each diagram, entities defined in another diagram appear with no attributes and name that diagram. Relationship lines run from the referenced row to the row that stores the foreign key; ||--o{ is composition (the parent owns the child), ||..o{ a reference or a polymorphic link resolved by a type column plus an id. The deal lifecycle has three diagrams: 3a is the deal and its collection, 3b the conversion and its exceptions, 3c the settlement. Appendix A reconciles the model with the FRS; Appendix B is the data dictionary.

1 · Configuration domain

A Client is the commercial relationship NPL contracts with; a Project is one arrangement with it and owns its configuration. Partners are global counterparties; how a partner is used in this project is the partner configuration block — fees, vehicles, endpoints, destination approvals and rebate terms hang off it. Counterparty receivers are organised in receiver groups, the unit entitlement is tracked on, and each receiving entity holds one or more accounts with a currency and rail.

Diagram 1a. PARTNER_CONFIG, PARTNER_PAIR, DESTINATION_APPROVAL, FEE_STRUCTURE are defined in Diagram 1b.

Diagram 1b. PROJECT, CURRENCY_PAIR, SENDER, RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT, OWN_WALLET are defined in Diagram 1a.

Notes

  • A Client is the commercial relationship NPL contracts with; a Project is one arrangement with it and owns its configuration. Counterparty receivers sit in receiver groups: every project has one default group and every counterparty receiver belongs to exactly one group. Entitlement is tracked per group, so payouts within a group are ordinary settlement and only payouts across groups are offsets; a project with a single group never has an offset.
  • A Receiver has a kind: counterparty for a client receiver; sender_return stands for a sender so refunds use the ordinary payout path and the partner's destination approval; partner_transit stands for a partner's collection endpoint so the hop of a two-leg route is an ordinary payout. sender_return and partner_transit receivers belong to no group (group_id is null). They never appear on forward deals or allow lists — both validate kind = counterparty — and a payout to them is attributed to the group of the leg that pays them, so no entitlement moves between groups on a refund or a hop. Groups exist for entitlement and offset accounting; refund exclusion is a receiver-kind rule, not a group.
  • A receiving entity holds one or more accounts, each with a currency and rail (EUR via SWIFT and EUR via SEPA are two accounts). An account is a bank account or a wallet (account_kind): a bank account carries bank_details_ref and a bank rail; a wallet carries network and address explicitly, mirroring the partner-side COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT, so addresses can be checksum-validated, checked against the rail, and found when the same address is registered with two partners. Destination approvals and settlement lines point at the account. No table stores actual bank details: bank_details_ref points at the external store.
  • Fees are per partner × pair (FEE_STRUCTURE under PARTNER_PAIR), so choosing the partner is part of pricing. PARTNER.disclosure_style records whether the partner's markup is visible; partner_fee_pct is known only for fee_on_market partners.
  • A partner operates through one or more legal vehicles (PARTNER_ENTITY: PT-tour, PT Global Inc); the deal stamps the vehicle at quote so paperwork names the right company. Each vehicle owns the endpoints a sender can pay into (COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT): kind = bank with a currency and bank_details_ref, or kind = wallet with network and address. The partner side therefore mirrors the client side — PARTNER_CONFIG → PARTNER_ENTITY → COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT as RECEIVER → RECEIVING_ENTITY → RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT. An endpoint also carries a nullable rail: a bank endpoint must have it before it becomes active, and a wallet may leave it null but must match network when it is set; the endpoint's kind must match the leg's collection_method. Cash-in has no endpoint record; the leg carries the city and the collection the token. The collected cash amount is rounded by the pair's cash_rounding option — truncate, nearest or round up — to cash_rounding_unit (100 / 500 / 1,000 by currency), the same menu as payout rounding.
  • Destination approval is per partner: DESTINATION_APPROVAL is an account of the project's receiving entity as registered with this partner, carrying the partner's approval status and the payout details the partner holds. Those details follow the account's kind: bank_details_ref for a bank account, network and address for a wallet. SETTLEMENT_SENDING_ENTITY is the narrative on an outgoing transfer; SETTLEMENT_RAIL is the bank/EMI that executes it; neither holds money. COLLECTION_SENDING_ENTITY is provenance only and never a payout destination.
  • OWN_WALLET has a role: reroute contingency (AQN-LT-Sub at Aquanow), own desk, or a collection bridge on a network a partner lacks, forwarded to the partner as a hop within the wallet's custody limit; PARTNER_CONFIG.applicable_for_reroute defines the alternate-partner set. PARTNER.supported_methods declares what a partner offers — cash and local deposits have no standing endpoint to read it from. WALLET_REGISTRY lists every known address with its owner and role. Under an own-desk partner configuration (is_own_desk, the NPL-GR game-reseller project) NPL itself is the converting party: its pairs are priced market plus NPL's markup and its collection endpoints are NPL's own wallets (COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT.own_wallet_id); the custody view reports every such balance.
  • Fees. A FEE_OVERRIDE may carry its own sender / receiver split instead of inheriting the structure's proportion. FEE_TIER rows under a structure price by the project's calendar-month volume; a leg that takes the month past a threshold is split across two tiers. customer_facing_fee_basis / customer_facing_fee_pct on the structure say what the customer's quote prints when it differs from the recorded parts; the printed "source rate" is derived at quote, never typed. CURRENCY_PAIR.amount_rounding is a menu — truncate, nearest or round up, to the unit or to rounding_unit — and a pair may have the same currency on both sides.
  • Who else earns on a deal. MARKUP_SHARE_PARTY / MARKUP_SHARE_RULE record a share NPL pays — or, with basis share_of_net_markup and party_kind client_party, the customer who provides a sub-account and shares NPL's markup (Raeen): the base is the leg's fee parts less its partner cost, rebates excluded, several parties may hold rules with different shares, and settlement_mode party_retains means the party holds the converted money and pays NPL the remainder monthly. PARTNER_REBATE_RULE records the rebate a partner pays NPL, with a basis (percentage of amount or of the partner's fee) and an optional scope by sender or fee structure; the rebate is NPL's alone and is reported as its own stream.
  • Cutoff, screening, single use. PARTNER.bank_cutoff_time (the partner's own clock, beside its rate expiry and holiday calendar), its per-day changes in PARTNER_CUTOFF_OVERRIDE (an agreed extension or an early close) and PARTNER_PAIR.needs_bank_lock drive same-day or next-day conversion and, on bank rails, same-day or next-day settlement. Cash legs carry their city (DEAL.cash_location) and cash rate versions theirs. WALLET_SCREENING records the screening of a sending or receiving wallet address, by Operations, and the endpoint's risk_band says which decisions may land on it. An endpoint or a receiving-entity account may be single_use, reserved for one deal (ad hoc local deposit accounts). HOLIDAY rows under the partner are the dates behind every "next business day"; MESSAGE_TEMPLATE is the versioned wording of outgoing messages and declares the fields it may print — a quote template prints sender-facing figures only.

2 · Rates domain

Diagram 2. RATE_SOURCE, CURRENCY_PAIR are defined in Diagram 1a; PARTNER_PAIR in 1b; DEAL in 3a; CONVERSION, BALANCE_CONVERSION in 3b.

Notes

  • The rate comparison for the day is created lazily by the first deal that needs it, one per partner × pair × date, and reused by every deal that day. A partner may give a new rate during the day, so one date can hold several versions. Rolling averages are built from confirmed versions only.
  • A version is breached when spread > avg_2w × (1 + variance_threshold_rel); quoting and conversion on that partner × pair freeze until Finance approves with a reason, rejects, or asks for a better rate. Versions are never overwritten; every deal leg, conversion and balance conversion references its exact version.
  • Cross-source slippage is a query over MARKET_RATE across sources for the same pair and window.
  • A version stores the rate as the partner quoted it (quoted_rate, quoted_direction); rate is normalised to the pair's direction and derived — 1 ÷ quoted when the directions differ — so Ali's 1.1738 becomes 0.851934 without a hand inversion, and a direction slip is caught by the breach check. Cash pairs are priced per location: INR cash in Delhi and in Mumbai are two versions on the same day.

Derived views (never stored)

ViewDefinition
PROJECT_BALANCE(project, partner, currency)PROJECT_BALANCE(project, partner, currency) = the balance of CL.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.DUE for the partner configuration: Σ debits − Σ credits over postings — conversions in, top-ups, make-goods, offsets and hops in, releases and offsets out — never a sum over deals (the definition summed conversions’ actual_out, which includes NPL’s margin, and had no term for the events). Was CLIENT_BALANCE. Also reports a pending column — the expected_out of legs whose rate is locked with the partner but whose money has not yet been collected or converted; a void removes it; pending is never a posting.
GROUP_ENTITLEMENT(group, currency)GROUP_ENTITLEMENT(group, currency) = Σ credits − Σ debits over CL.PROJECT.<CCY>.PAYABLE postings carrying receiver_group_id = the group: promises raised at collection and conversion, re-raised on a return or a short confirmation, re-denominated by an offset or a balance conversion, reduced by a release or a client loss share. A payout to a group-less receiver carries the paying leg’s group (SETTLEMENT_LINE.deal_id). Σ over a project’s groups = the PAYABLE balance = Σ client assets, per currency.
OFFSET(group, currency)OFFSET(group, currency) = GROUP_ENTITLEMENT; positive = owed, negative = holding another group's flow. Arises only when a counterparty receiver is paid from a leg attributed to another group; zero by construction in a single-group project. Carries Management approval and tighter aging.
CUSTODY(own_wallet)CUSTODY(own_wallet) = Σ collections into the own wallet under open reroutes + Σ recovered dues resting there + Σ own-desk client balances + Σ bridge collections not yet forwarded − Σ forwarded or paid out; each row with deal, reason, role and age. The standing control on money in NPL’s hands.
INVOICE_BALANCE(invoice)INVOICE_BALANCE(invoice): for a vendor invoice, INVOICE.amount − Σ SETTLEMENT_LINE.obligation_discharged over released lines not returned (a payment discharges on release); for a resale invoice, INVOICE.amount − Σ DEAL_GROUP.invoice_amount over the groups that collected it with a verified collection. Σ VENDOR_PAYABLE = Σ vendor-invoice balances; Σ RESALE_RECEIVABLE = Σ resale-invoice balances (
PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME(project, month, currency)PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME(project, month, currency) = Σ DEAL.amount_in over forward legs of the project collected in the calendar month, in the tier’s volume currency. Read at quote to choose the FEE_TIER; stamped on the leg as tier_volume_basis.
CLIENT_POSITION(client, currency)CLIENT_POSITION(client, currency) = Σ over the client’s projects of PROJECT_BALANCE (per partner), GROUP_ENTITLEMENT, CUSTODY, and the period’s earnings (EARN_GROSS) and rebates (EARN_REBATE) from postings — the client-level report that project = client made impossible. Compared with CLIENT.exposure_ceiling when set. Its one-currency total is a REPORTING_VALUE, an estimate at the latest market rate.
WALLET_REGISTRY(network, address)WALLET_REGISTRY(network, address) = every wallet address the model knows, with its owner and role: the partners’ receiving wallets (COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT kind wallet, with risk_band), NPL’s own wallets (OWN_WALLET with role), receivers’ wallets (RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT kind wallet, with their DESTINATION_APPROVALs) and the sender addresses seen in WALLET_SCREENING with their latest decision. A view, never a second copy of an address: it answers which networks a partner accepts, which wallet is the bridge, and whether an address was seen before under another owner — the FRS ‘wallet registry’.
REPORTING_VALUE(subject, currency, as_of)REPORTING_VALUE(subject, currency, as_of) = any per-currency figure of the model — a PROJECT_BALANCE, a CLIENT_POSITION line, a month’s collection volume (PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME), earnings and rebates from postings, custody — multiplied by the latest MARKET_RATE of the platform pair for that currency (its PAIR_RATE_SOURCE chain), with the market_rate_id and captured_at it used and a stale flag when the rate is older than reporting_rate_max_age_min. An estimate for display: the figures in each currency stay the facts, the converted total is a view over them at the moment it is read. Serves project-level and overall collection volumes, earnings and current balances in one currency.
RESELLER_MARGIN(resale_invoice)RESELLER_MARGIN(resale invoice) = resale INVOICE.amount − the amount of INVOICE.vendor_invoice_id, in the invoice currency, equal to RESELL_REVENUE − RESELL_COST posted for the pair: NPL-GR’s game reseller revenue, fixed when the two invoices are posted and untouched by anything the remittance side does (;
REMITTANCE_MARGIN(deal)REMITTANCE_MARGIN(deal) = EARN_GROSS (net of markup shares) − EXP_PARTNER ± VAR_FX_TIMING − EXP_BANKFEE − EXP_NETWORK − EXP_ROUNDING on the deal’s postings, in the converted currency: NPL’s remittance earnings on one deal, including the forex result of instalments paid at different days’ rates.
NPL_PROFIT(scope, period, currency)NPL_PROFIT(scope, period, currency) = remittance earnings (EARN_GROSS + EARN_REBATE − EXP_PARTNER − EXP_BANKFEE − EXP_NETWORK − EXP_ROUNDING − EXP_LOSS ± VAR_CONVERSION ± VAR_CUTOFF ± VAR_RATE_HONOUR ± VAR_FX_TIMING) + reseller earnings (RESELL_REVENUE − RESELL_COST), each callable on its own and together, by project, partner, pair or month, per currency; one figure across currencies is a REPORTING_VALUE.

Notes

  • Every deal belongs to a deal group. DEAL_GROUP is the client-facing instruction: the pair as the sender sees it, the sender rate, fee, reference and entry mode. A plain single-partner deal is a group of one leg; a route that needs two partners (INR → USDT at Ali, USDT → EUR at Jeton) has two forward legs; a rejected payout is unwound with a return leg.
  • Legs. leg_type forward or return; funding_source collection, prior_leg (leg 2 of a route, no collection) or returned_settlement (a return leg). Priced once and partner fixed at quote hold per leg. Attribution is to the receiver group: set at quote on the first forward leg, inherited by leg n of a route from leg n−1 and by a return leg from its parent leg. The receiver is optional until settlement.
  • Two entry modes as before: collect-first legs are born in state Collected with priced_at = conversion time; quote-first legs carry sent / valid / grace timestamps and a late decision. An estimate-first mode gives an indicative figure and prices at conversion.
  • Conversion has exactly one owner: a deal leg or a BALANCE_CONVERSION. The receiver-side fee is taken at conversion. Amounts are rounded at conversion by the pair's option; a dropped fraction (rounding_residual, signed) stays client money in the balance and pays out when it reaches a unit, an amount added by rounding up is NPL's cost. NPL's margin is captured at conversion and is never again at risk from a return or a forward.
  • Balance conversion is NPL converting a client's held balance (5K SGD → USDT to fund a 15K USDT payout): Finance-initiated, Management-approved, no sender, receiver or collection, same rate machinery, markup by FEE_DECISION. It names the receiver group it serves; ENTITLEMENT_REATTRIBUTION moves that group's entitlement to the new currency, and any excess over the group's entitlement is booked as an approved offset.
  • Reroute is the only way partner or partner entity change after quote. Forwarding is forward_full or forward_and_recover_dues: NPL nets what the alternate partner owes it (EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE) against the funds forwarded, within the outstanding receivable, with the partner's agreement recorded. Post-collection outcome is via the own wallet or a refund to the sender.
  • One settlement model: SETTLEMENT drains one partner's holding into one or many SETTLEMENT_LINEs, rounded as the pair says. Under settlement_policy to_zero the balance after release is less than one unit; under hold_allowed the balance may rest at the partner within the project's exposure cap.
  • A line paying a counterparty receiver whose group differs from the paying leg's attributed group is an offset, created by the same action, with Management approval and tighter aging. A line paying a sender_return or partner_transit receiver is never an offset: those receivers have no group, and the line debits the group of the leg it names in deal_id.
  • Rejected payout. When the receiving or intermediary bank rejects a transfer, SETTLEMENT_RETURN records the returned amount, bank fee and reason; the line's outcome becomes returned, a reversing ledger transaction puts the money back into the client's balance and the paying leg's group entitlement, and BANK_FEE_EVENT books the bounce fee. The money then stays in balance for later payouts, or funds a return leg — attributed to the same group — that converts back and pays the sender's return receiver.
  • Fee decisions. FEE_DECISION is a one-off, approved decision on a single subject: markup applied or waived on a return leg or balance conversion, a network-fee override on a refund, a bank-fee treatment override on one settlement. Standing rules stay in FEE_STRUCTURE and FEE_OVERRIDE.
  • CONFIRMATION is full or short; a short confirmation opens a SHORTFALL topped up by a later settlement or an explicit separate payout — cash found short at hand-over included. Rounding differences no longer land here. MARKUP_SHARE_ACCRUAL and PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL accrue per deal under their rules; a party_retains markup-share accrual is a receivable from the party, reconciled monthly like a rebate; rebates are reconciled monthly against the partner's statement, which covers NPLify deals only.
  • Pricing stamps. A leg stamps the override and the base tier that priced it; a leg that crosses a tier threshold holds two DEAL_FEE_TIER portions and a blended fee. The deal group stamps the customer-facing fee and rate the quote printed. On a pair that needs a bank lock the leg records rate_locked_at and conversion_due_date: locked before the partner's cutoff it converts the same day, otherwise the next business day at that day's version; the sender's figures are write-once, NPL absorbs the difference as a cutoff-timing variance, and a conversion whose next-day rate breaches the margin is deferred with a reason. The client balance view shows the locked leg's converted value as pending from the lock; a void removes it. QUOTE_PACKAGE is the record of what was sent for a deal group — template version, channel, printed figures, sent_at, hash — one row per issue; a quote-first leg is Sent only when a package has sent_at, re-issues are new rows, a new price is a new deal group.
  • Invoices. INVOICE is an obligation in its own currency — a vendor's EUR invoice a reseller customer pays in THB or USDT, in parts, over days. A deal group names the invoice it pays (advance, then balance); each payout line records how much of the obligation it discharged and the market snapshot used; INVOICE_BALANCE is the open remainder.
  • Cash and crypto parts. A cash part carries the token (the local-currency bill whose serial identifies the agent), the agent's contact and the partner's count; the leg carries the city, which also selects the rate version. A crypto part carries the sender's declared address and the screening that admitted it, unless the project skips up-front screening.
  • Loss events. LOSS_EVENT records money lost after it was verified or released — a frozen local account, cash short that cannot be recovered, a wrong-chain transfer — on either side, by any method, for a partial or full amount, with the loss split across sender, NPL, partner and client. The whole loss is booked to NPL and the client made whole in one transaction (source LossEvent; MAKEGOOD / LOSS_PAYABLE when it cannot be funded at once); Management approves the split and each share is a separate LOSS_RECOVERY posting; the collection part stays verified and is reversed only when the deal is unwound.

4 · Ledger & controls domain

Diagram 4. OWN_WALLET, RECEIVER, SENDER, MARKUP_SHARE_PARTY are defined in Diagram 1a; PARTNER_CONFIG in 1b; COLLECTION, INVOICE in 3a; CONVERSION, BALANCE_CONVERSION, REROUTE, EARNINGS_OFFSET in 3b; SETTLEMENT, SETTLEMENT_RETURN, CONFIRMATION, BANK_FEE_EVENT, MARKUP_SHARE_ACCRUAL, PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL, LOSS_EVENT, LOSS_RECOVERY in 3c.

Notes

  • Client due balances are held as one account per project × partner × currency (CL.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.DUE); group entitlement is a view, not an account. holder_type never includes a settlement rail or narrative entity.
  • Ownership moves between client and company only at named events — margin recognition at conversion, the two sides of an earnings offset, the forex true-ups of invoice lines, fees NPL absorbs or covers, top-ups, make-wholes, make-goods and the client's loss share — and every transaction balances per owner as well as per currency. NPL never advances money to a receiver, and withholding on a reroute is not a separate event because the margin is always captured by whichever partner converts.
  • Recover dues on a reroute posts own-wallet cash against the earnings receivable at the partner: company money on both sides, no income.
  • Transaction sources: Collection, Conversion, BalanceConversion, Settlement, SettlementReturn, Confirmation, BankFeeEvent, Reroute, MarkupShare, Rebate, LossEvent, LossRecovery, Invoice, EarningsOffset, Adjustment. Account purposes include PAYABLE, SHARE_PAYABLE, SHARE_RECEIVABLE, REBATE_RECEIVABLE, LOSS_RECEIVABLE, MAKEGOOD / LOSS_PAYABLE, EARN_GROSS, EARN_REBATE, the four VAR_ accounts, FX_RESULT, the reseller purposes (RESELL_REVENUE, RESELL_COST, VENDOR_PAYABLE, RESALE_RECEIVABLE, REMIT_CLAIM), EXP_ROUNDING and EXP_LOSS; ADVANCE and INTRANSIT do not exist. Cost components include share, rebate, rounding, fx_timing, cutoff_timing, loss and resale.
  • Three streams NPL never mixes. Earnings on deals post to EARN_GROSS at conversion; a partner's rebate posts to EARN_REBATE and is never in the base a client party shares; NPL's remainder from a party that holds the converted funds sits in SHARE_RECEIVABLE until the party pays it. The cost of rounding up is EXP_ROUNDING. A loss is booked to EXP_LOSS in full first and the client made whole; the partner's and the sender's agreed shares are LOSS_RECEIVABLE owed to NPL, the client's share is a partial reversal of the make-good, and what remains in EXP_LOSS is NPL's own share. Own-desk deals use the ordinary partner-coded accounts with the own-desk configuration as holder and EXP_PARTNER zero by construction.
  • One system-settings area: SYSTEM_SETTING holds NPL-wide, Management-approved keys — the reporting currency, its staleness limit, the operating time zone; ROLE holds the user roles and ROLE_RIGHT what each may initiate and approve per controlled action, with the role added on escalation; platform-scope CURRENCY_PAIRs carry the conversion rates through the ordinary rate-source chain. REPORTING_VALUE converts any per-currency figure into the reporting currency at the latest market rate of its platform pair, as a display-only estimate that carries the rate it used. APPROVAL, AUDIT_LOG and RECORD_LOCK are modelled once and apply to all master data. Approver ≠ initiator on every approval; Operations never sees derived economics. Approval actions include price_quote, extend_quote_validity, refund_to_third_party, cross_group_payout, balance_conversion, recover_dues, cover_bank_fee, raise_fee_cap, enable_own_desk, approve_loss_split, override_screening_reject and earnings_offset (ROLE_RIGHT rows). cross_group_payout never fires on a line paying a sender_return or partner_transit receiver. Wallet screening itself is an Operations action, not an approval.

Markup shared with a party — was INTRODUCER / REFERRAL_*MARKUP_SHARE_PARTY, MARKUP_SHARE_RULE, MARKUP_SHARE_ACCRUAL; purpose SHARE_PAYABLE
Approved destination — was SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATIONDESTINATION_APPROVAL
Sender pays / receiver pays; lowest and highest markup; customer-facing calculation; fee on top of market / fee inside its rate; agent ratesender_pays_pct, receiver_pays_pct; min_markup_pct, max_markup_pct; customer_facing_fee_basis / _pct / _rate; partner_fee_pct with fee_on_market / fee_in_rate; rate_basis market / agent_rate
Client balance at a partner — was CLIENT_BALANCEPROJECT_BALANCE(project, partner, currency); the client-level roll-up is CLIENT_POSITION
System / reporting currencySYSTEM_SETTING reporting_currency + platform-scope CURRENCY_PAIRs (their PAIR_RATE_SOURCE) + REPORTING_VALUE view, an estimate at the latest market rate
User roles (Operations, Finance, Management)ROLE rows referenced by USER.role_id, with one ROLE_RIGHT row per role × controlled action (initiate / approve / escalate); rights per role in the Roles & Visibility Matrix

A.2 Deviations from the FRS (classified)

FRS statementModelClassification
P1 — no custodyNo custody except under an approved reroute or in an own-desk project (NPL-GR); OWN_WALLET + REROUTE for contingency, and the custody view as the controlDecided (answered;, 9 October 2026)
P3 — partner books never mixAccounts per partner never net; alternate partner on reroute; post-collection transfer only if confirmsDecided (answered: reroute with recover dues; partner accounts never net)
Strict Client → Entity → Sender, one parent eachRECEIVER_GROUP → RECEIVER → RECEIVING_ENTITY → account; SENDER with a group allow-list; FRS project = one default groupGeneralisation per NPL instruction
Beyond grace → re-quote alwayslate_collection_policy per project; FRS project keeps requotePer NPL instruction (Sept 2026)
Sender always priced on KrakenFEE_STRUCTURE.rate_basis; FRS project = marketGeneralisation
One settlement per deal, full amountAccumulate → settle the balance rounded as the pair says (residual carried), or hold within the exposure cap where the project allowsGeneralisation
Partner fixed at quoteSame, except under REROUTEConsistent
Bank fee → shortfall → top-upcarry_forward is the FRS behaviour; waived / absorbed addedPer NPL instruction
Registry-only destinationsDESTINATION_APPROVAL.approval_status — FRS project has all approvedGeneralisation
AQN-LT-Sub offset-settled collectionsOWN_WALLET at Aquanow; pass-through is a two-leg deal group or a reroute via the own wallet; also NPL-GR's own-desk collection endpointResolved
